captions.text: This is our hall, rebuilt from the floor plan and measured with our phones on 9 November. You're on a call over 4G: our phones found LTE here, not 5G.
Infinet found the venue's free Wi-Fi. It shows a sign-in page, so the call stays on 4G for now. Tap Sign in by the phone (or press L).
Signed in. Infinet checks the Wi-Fi again and moves the call onto it: Wi-Fi first, so no mobile data is spent. 4G stays ready.
About 20 phone hotspots and 11 other devices at any spot in this hall, as our phones heard them, and 6 networks on every venue access point. Infinet never joins strangers.
Stand 31: that's us. Press N to see the hall's Wi-Fi and 4G as we measured them.

notes: Survey: 27 points by realme RMX3760 on 2026-11-09 (file 202611091346); 1 other file(s) used as a cross-check.
Venue infrastructure: 50 radio groups heard; 27 placed (5 GHz at 5+ points, 2.4 GHz at 9+); the exponent comes from the 18 radios heard at 15+ points.
Path-loss exponent for the hall: n = 2 (searched 2.0–3.0, free space or more; RMS error 3.6 dB over those radios), radios at 10 m.
Guest network: the open network on 27 of 27 radios (both bands), shown as "Venue-Free-WiFi".
Fit error per band (RMS): 5 GHz 3.8 dB, 2.4 GHz 10.3 dB.
Placed 27 venue radios (20 at 5 GHz, EIRP -1.1 to 14.7 dBm; 7 at 2.4 GHz, EIRP -4.1 to 3.5 dBm).
Venue Wi-Fi sign-in page: ASSUMPTION. UAE public Wi-Fi asks visitors to register before use; the survey did not join it.

Everyone else's networks, placed one by one: 64 phone hotspots (randomised addresses; 19 Wi-Fi 4, 2 Wi-Fi 5, 40 Wi-Fi 6, 3 Wi-Fi 7) and 35 fixed devices (8 Wi-Fi 4, 7 Wi-Fi 5, 16 Wi-Fi 6, 4 Wi-Fi 7). 48 hotspots and 20 devices heard at 3+ points are placed with their own EIRP; the 31 heard at 1–2 points use the typical EIRP of their kind (hotspots 4.6 dBm, devices 9.6 dBm). Their own loss exponent n = 2 (searched 2.0–4.0 on the 42 heard at 8+ points, misses included); phones at 1.2 m, devices at 1.5 m (ASSUMPTION). 68 distinct names, kept only as ids.

Placed networks against the survey: RMS signal error 4.5 dB over 843 readings; each is on air for the share of time it was heard where it should have been audible (median 26 %), so per point the model hears 20.2 hotspots and 12.2 devices on average (median over the points), the survey heard 20 and 11. Scan floor -78 dBm (the weakest 2 % the phone reported).
Mobile: serving cell LTE band 3 (one PCI at every point), RSRP -81 to -69 dBm, median -78 dBm. The simulated link stays 5G with this RSRP (the second phone is 4G-only, so LTE is all it could show).
Mobile technology: the survey phone was registered on LTE at every point (no 5G cell reported), so the hall shows it as 4G.

Mobile site fitted 125 m away at bearing 170° (UMa, 1.8 GHz, 30 m, hall O2I high): RMS error 3.8 dB after a calibration of +27.6 dB. The measured signal is that much stronger than an outdoor site would give through the hall's walls under TR 38.901, so the hall most likely has indoor antennas; the offset makes the site match what we measured.
Cross-check (Nothing A063, 33.4, 41.8): strongest venue 5 GHz -61 dBm measured, -64 dBm from the fitted radios; 18 hotspots and 13 devices heard, 22 and 12 in the model.
